stem: The amount of a dye, in milligrams, remaining in a water sample \(h\) hours after the dye is added is modeled by \(D(h) = 240\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{h}{6}}\). Which of the following is closest to the percent decrease in the amount of dye each hour?
solution: The model halves the amount every 6 hours. The factor for one hour is \(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{1}{6}}\).
With a calculator, \(0.5^{1/6} \approx 0.891\), so about \(89.1\%\) of the dye remains after each hour.
The decrease per hour is about \(100\% - 89.1\% = 10.9\%\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is \(50\% \div 6\). Percent changes over equal time periods multiply; they are not shared out evenly by division.
explanation.B: Correct. The hourly factor is \(0.5^{1/6} \approx 0.891\), so the amount decreases by about \(10.9\%\) each hour.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The amount decreases by \(50\%\) every 6 hours, not every hour.
explanation.D: Incorrect. About \(89.1\%\) of the dye remains after each hour; the question asks for the percent decrease, which is \(100\% - 89.1\%\).

verify:
r = 1 - Rational(1, 2)**Rational(1, 6)
assert abs(N(r) - 0.109) < 0.0005
assert abs(value(choices[answer]) - r) < 0.0005
assert all(abs(value(choices[k]) - r) > 0.01 for k in choices if k != answer)
